hero.lead: A nation of 9.2 million in the Alps, with forest across almost half its land and eight tenths of its power renewable, whose debt agency plans €43 to €47 billion of federal bonds in 2026.

register.name: Federal bonds, 2026
register.detail: Austrian Federal Financing Agency (OeBFA) · annual review 2025, 20 April 2026 · 2025: €45.0bn issued
register.note: Planned issuance for 2026, against €45.0 billion of federal bonds issued in 2025
register.text: Planned issuance of federal bonds by the Republic of Austria in 2026, with a moderate rise of €2 to €4 billion in short-term instruments. In 2025 the Republic issued €45.0 billion of federal bonds.

register.name: Bundesschatz
register.detail: Federal Ministry of Finance · 20 April 2026 · more than 170,000 accounts
register.note: Over €10 billion invested after two years; almost €2 billion in green Bundesschatz
register.text: A savings product through which citizens and public bodies lend directly to the Republic, with more than 170,000 accounts opened since its launch. Almost €2 billion of the volume invested by private savers is in green Bundesschatz, which finances public spending and investment that drive the green transformation and adaptation to climate change.

register.name: Green federal financing, 2025
register.detail: OeBFA · green bonds in four transactions, €2.61bn · green Bundesschatz €650M · about €6.0bn planned for 2026
register.note: €6,133.5 million allocated to eligible green federal spending, 47.4% of it to clean transportation
register.text: New green issuance by the Republic of Austria in 2025, through green federal bonds, green Bundesschatz and green bonds in Swiss francs. The Green Investor Report allocates €6,133.5 million to eligible federal spending, including €1,499.4 million for renewable energy and €289.2 million for sustainable water and wastewater management, which serve the energy and water standards.

register.name: Recovery and resilience plan
register.detail: European Union · non-repayable support · fourth payment request €370.4M (24 March 2026) · final payment €306M disbursed
register.note: The Commission has disbursed €306 million on Austria’s final payment request
register.text: Non-repayable EU support of €3,961 million for Austria’s reforms and investments under the Recovery and Resilience Facility, paid in instalments against agreed milestones and targets. The Commission has disbursed €306 million to Austria on its final payment request.

register.name: Burgenland Energie wind and solar portfolio
register.detail: EIB · €250M loan signed 2025 · €20M added 13 October 2026 · some 2,000 MW of wind and solar by 2030
register.note: The largest portfolio for solar and wind power plants in Austria
register.text: EIB loans to Burgenland Energie, the electricity supplier of the region of Burgenland and Austria’s largest wind power and photovoltaics company, for a portfolio of some 2,000 MW of wind and solar generation by 2030. A €20 million loan announced on 13 October 2026 follows a €250 million loan in 2025; together they serve the energy standard with clean power.

register.name: Volksbank Wien social and affordable housing
register.detail: EIB · intermediated framework loan · signed 3 September 2026 · total cost about €420M
register.note: About 1,600 new social and affordable housing units
register.text: An EIB framework loan through Volksbank Wien to support the financing of social and affordable housing investments in Austria, for about 1,600 new homes at a total cost of about €420 million. It serves the shelter standard.

register.name: Hypo Tirol Bank loan for SMEs and mid-caps
register.detail: EIB · signed July 2026 · matched by €50M from Hypo Tirol Bank · at least 60% for SMEs · 20% for climate action
register.note: €100 million in all for small and medium-sized enterprises, mid-caps and public-sector entities
register.text: A €50 million EIB loan to Hypo Tirol Bank, matched by the bank, making €100 million available for investment by small and medium-sized enterprises, mid-caps and public-sector entities, including tourism, hospitality and regional businesses. At least 60% goes to SMEs and 20% is earmarked for climate action, including energy-efficient buildings and renovation; it serves the livelihood standard.

register.name: PÜSPÖK super-hybrid renewable park, Burgenland
register.detail: EIB · announced 1 June 2026 · mainly a direct loan to PÜSPÖK, 10% via Erste Bank · wind, solar and battery storage at four sites
register.note: Total EIB support for the Burgenland project now around €200 million
register.text: EIB financing for PÜSPÖK, an Austrian renewable energy company, to expand hybrid sites in Burgenland that combine wind power, photovoltaics and battery storage through shared infrastructure at four sites, including Nickelsdorf, the second-largest super-hybrid park of its kind in Europe. It serves the energy standard with clean and stored power.

register.name: LINZ AG energy and water networks
register.detail: EIB · project 20240660 · signed 16 April 2026 · district heating and cooling, water and wastewater
register.note: Services for around 400,000 people and numerous businesses in the Linz area
register.text: A €200 million EIB loan to LINZ AG, the utility of the city of Linz, to integrate energy, water and wastewater networks into a single system that will be greener and more efficient, with district heating and cooling, heat pumps that recover waste heat and upgrades throughout the water cycle. It serves the water and energy standards for around 400,000 people.

register.name: Affordable housing in Salzburg and Tyrol
register.detail: EIB · up to €100M to Salzburger Sparkasse (signed 16 July 2024) and up to €75M to Tiroler Sparkasse · announced 11 September 2024
register.note: Up to 1,000 new homes in Salzburg and 750 in Innsbruck by 2028
register.text: EIB framework loans to two Austrian savings banks to finance new affordable housing, within total investment of €200 million in Salzburg and €150 million in Tyrol. Up to 1,000 new homes in Salzburg and 750 in Innsbruck can be financed by 2028, which serves the shelter standard.

assets.heading: Five assets no balance sheet counts.

items.name: The Forest
items.label: Of the land under forest, 2024
items.text: Standing forest that stores carbon and water, and can earn as it stands.
items.alt: Forest on an Alpine mountainside in Austria

items.name: The Clean Grid
items.label: Of electricity from renewable sources, 2021
items.text: Power from water, wind and sun already flows; every new connection can be clean.
items.alt: A hydroelectric dam and power lines in the Austrian Alps

items.name: The Fresh Water
items.label: Renewable fresh water a person, 2022
items.text: Rain and rivers renewed every year: power, irrigation and drinking water.
items.alt: A clear Alpine river in an Austrian valley

items.name: The People
items.label: Citizens, 2025
items.text: 14.1% are under fifteen: the workforce and the market of the next generation.
items.alt: A Vienna street with a tram in the evening

items.name: The Farmland
items.label: Of the land in agriculture, 2023
items.text: Land that can feed the nation and earn abroad, valued and financed against its harvest.
items.alt: Farmland and vineyards in Lower Austria

items.name: SOMA Sozialmärkte (Wiener Hilfswerk)
items.text: Social markets in Vienna, run by the Wiener Hilfswerk with SOMA Österreich & Partner, that sell low-cost food to residents with an income below the at-risk-of-poverty threshold. The market in Neubau is a social enterprise that offers fixed-term jobs, with the support of the public employment service, to women and men far from the labour market.

items.name: neunerhaus
items.text: A Vienna organisation that has supported people who can no longer afford housing for over two decades, through Housing First and a health centre with a medical practice, nursing and a dental practice. In 2025 its teams supported 575 households in Housing First and mobile supported housing, and its health centre saw 5,317 patients.

items.name: OurPower Energiegenossenschaft
items.text: An energy cooperative owned by over 1,000 members whose digital marketplace has, since 2019, let producers sell their electricity directly in their region and across Austria; it also offers a service package to set up and run energy communities. At the end of 2025 it had 476 producers on the marketplace and 1,414 customers.

items.name: Grow Together
items.text: Supports families facing severe psychosocial challenges from the birth of a child onward, through attachment-based, mobile support services. A winner of the Get active Social Business Award in 2013, it was honoured again at the award’s twentieth anniversary in September 2026.

items.name: magdas HOTEL
items.text: A hotel next to the Vienna Prater, run jointly by hotel industry professionals and refugees, by magdas, the social business of Caritas of the Archdiocese of Vienna, with every room designed in upcycling style. Caritas Vienna’s impact report for 2025 names it as a place of meaningful work for people with a refugee background.

items.name: NACHBARINNEN
items.text: Supports socially isolated women through guidance in their native language, educational assistance, outreach counselling and pathways to employment. A winner of the Get active Social Business Award in 2013, it was honoured again at the award’s twentieth anniversary in September 2026.
